note: Based on the original description in Hagen 1858, Monographie der Termiten (Linnaea Entomologica 12, pp. 222—224), a Latin diagnosis with a detailed German account. Hagen states explicitly that the species was collected and named by Bates ('Termes arenarius Bates mss.') and is first described and published by him; the original account is placed in Termes, now in Nasutitermes. Locality: Obispo, Isthmus of Panama, collected from a tree in March (month 3); there is also soldier material from Santarem (Amazon River). Fractions in the original account (e.g. the proportions of the 6th sternite, the ratios of leg segments) are damaged in the scan and are not cited.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate pale leather-yellow with a chestnut head, the vertex with a pale red diffuse patch; wings dull greyish yellow with leather-yellow marginal vein, the apical curve of the costa weak, the media sending 3 branches to the posterior margin near the apex, the submedia with few and sparse branches (6—7). Head nearly quadrate, flat, densely covered with fine hairs; compound eyes rather large but flat, ocelli small, separated from the compound eyes by more than their own diameter, the two joined by a slightly curved elevation running across the frons. The soldier is of the 'nasute type with unenlarged mandibles', about 3 mm long, about half of which is the polished dark chestnut head.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Pale leather-yellow, head chestnut, the vertex with a pale red indistinct patch; mouthparts, antennae and gizzard leather-yellow; wings dull greyish yellow, marginal vein leather-yellow. Size as in T. lividus, but darker in colour and with a thicker head and thorax. Head densely covered with very fine hairs, large, nearly quadrate, flat; compound eyes rather large but flat, not very prominent; at a distance from the compound eyes almost greater than their own diameter lie the small ocelli, joined by a slightly curved elevation running across the frons; above the elevation the frons is depressed, with a finely engraved yellow line along the median suture. Anterior margin concave, with two depressed points on each side. Clypeus elevated, divided in the middle. Antennae 16-segmented, as in T. lividus. Pronotum narrower than the head, shaped much as in T. lividus but wider and shorter, the sides not rounded but merely oblique, the anterior corners much blunter and hardly bent downwards. Body wider, shorter and more oval; the 6th sternite of the female shorter and more oblong. Legs as in T. lividus. Wing shape and venation as in T. lividus, differing in the weaker apical curve of the costa, the media sending 3 veins to the posterior margin near the apex, and the fewer and sparser veins of the submedia (6—7). Head and thorax polished, the whole body covered with very fine dense hairs. Measurements: length with wings 14 mm, body length 6 mm, wing expanse 27 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Bates labelled several specimens as soldiers, belonging to the then unexplained 'nasute type with unenlarged mandibles'. The specimen is strongly shrivelled, about 3 mm long, about half of which is the polished dark chestnut head; the rest is coloured like the worker, the antennae slightly brownish. Head shape hard to describe: the occiput strongly contracted, almost spherical; nasus shorter than the head, pointed, conical, its upper margin forming a straight continuation of the vertex. Antennae long, 14-segmented, all segments except the 2nd rather elongate. Legs very long and slender. Pronotum very small and short, the upturned anterior part wider than long, gently rounded, without a notch. Hagen also describes a shrivelled 4 mm specimen (probably the soldier of this species): head yellow-red, nasus brownish, antennae and legs white, body grey; head strongly convex, long-quadrate, almost twice as long as wide; conical nasus slightly shorter than the head, slightly bent down, its truncate tip closed by a white membrane; sabre-shaped mandibles crossed, almost reaching the tip of the nasus, curved only at the blade, not very pointed, without teeth on the inner margin, symmetrical left and right; labrum oval, pointed; antennae 14-segmented, slightly longer than the head, the segments shorter than in the previous form and cylindrical; pronotum far narrower than the head, the upturned anterior part larger than the posterior and rounded, semicircular, the two posterior corners drawn out into long points; legs long and slender.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Hagen saw only one rather poor specimen slightly longer than 3 mm. Head dark chestnut, the sutures whitish; thorax and body paler, antennae, legs and gizzard yellow-white. Head large, sparsely hairy, polished, shaped as in the alate: quadrate, rounded posteriorly, flat; frons less deeply depressed, only slightly concave at the end of the median suture; a shallow impression towards the mouth. No compound eyes. Antennae lost. Pronotum far narrower than the head, the upturned anterior part equal in size to the posterior, rounded, twice as wide as long, with a median notch on the anterior margin; the lateral corners of the posterior part drawn out into long points bent downwards. Meso- and metanota transversely oval, strongly rounded and larger posteriorly.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Female (queen): 3 dried specimens, body length 22 mm, width 4 mm (abdomen distended). They do not differ in any respect from the two wingless males recorded as 'kings' and from the 6 alates of both sexes. Nymph: numerous specimens of both sexes, 4—6 mm long, pale yellow throughout, the compound eyes not yet pigmented, head and pronotum identical with the alate, wings not reaching the end of the abdomen.
